deep.reconstruction:
The page holds a single pencil figure numbered '11' at the upper left. The '12' at the lower left is the archive page number.

The figure is an arrangement of FIVE straight (pseudo-)lines in general position:
(1) one from upper left down to lower right;
(2) one from the left, gently curving, out to the right;
(3) one from lower left up to the right;
(4) one from lower left steeply up to the top;
(5) a nearly vertical one.
The short stroke in the middle looks like a retouch or an aborted line, not a sixth line.

The bounded cells: a 5-line affine arrangement in general position has C(4,2) = 6 bounded cells. Grothendieck writes the number of sides inside each one: 3, ?, 5, ?, 3, 3. The two marks transcribed '2[?]' must be 4s, because no 2-gons occur in a simple line arrangement.

The unbounded cells: there are 2n = 10 of them, each labelled q_i. Going round clockwise from the upper left, the labels read q2, q5, q1, q3, q4, q2, q5, q1, q3, q6. This is period 5 except that 'q6' stands where 'q4' is expected. So the labels are faces of the arrangement in the PROJECTIVE plane: opposite unbounded affine regions are identified through the line at infinity.

The projective count then works out:
- 6 bounded + 5 unbounded = 11 = 1 + C(5,2) faces, which is the '11' heading the figure. The previous page also ends with '11'.
- Face sizes must sum to 2E = 40.
- The unique simple arrangement of 5 pseudolines in the projective plane has 5 triangles, 5 quadrilaterals and 1 pentagon: 15 + 20 + 5 = 40.
- The bounded faces give 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 5, so the five unbounded projective faces q1..q5 must be 2 triangles and 3 quadrilaterals.

The page thus serves a census of simple arrangements of pseudolines (here n = 5) and their combinatorial invariants. These are face vectors, the identification of faces at infinity, and probably automorphism or labelling counts; the previous page has 48 = 2·4!, 5!/(2·4!) and 12 = 8×3×2/4. The next page moves on to metric or inequality conditions on a configuration of points (a + a' ≤ 2, b + b' ≥ 2), likely about stretchability or realizations.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The label 'q6' on the left unbounded region is inconsistent with the projective identification, which requires q4. Either Grothendieck wrote q4 ambiguously or he slipped.

ideas.what: Drawing a simple arrangement of 5 lines and recording the polygon type of every cell; the cell count 11 = 1 + C(5,2) in the projective plane.
ideas.modern_name: Face vector / cell census of simple projective (pseudo)line arrangements; the unique simple arrangement of 5 pseudolines (5 triangles, 5 quadrilaterals, 1 pentagon).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Steiner 1826 for counts; Levi 1926 for pseudolines; Grünbaum, Arrangements and Spreads 1972)

ideas.what: Labelling unbounded affine regions so that opposite regions carry the same name, i.e. passing to faces of the projective arrangement.
ideas.modern_name: Projective closure of an affine arrangement (antipodal identification / line at infinity)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine illustrative sketch of the unique simple 5-line arrangement with its face sizes, consistent with known counts. Its only interest is documentary: it shows Grothendieck working through small cases of pseudoline arrangements around 1981.
transcription_corrections: The two marks transcribed '2[?]' inside cells are almost certainly '4' (quadrilaterals). The cell labels read 3, 4, 5, 4, 3, 3 (bounded faces), not 3, 2, 5, 2, 3, 3.

The q_i are labels of the 10 unbounded regions, in clockwise order from the upper left: q2, q5, q1, q3, q4, q2, q5, q1, q3, q6 (the last presumably meant as q4). They are not line names. The two lists in the machine transcription mix large and small labels.
'11' at the upper left is the figure/case heading (= number of projective cells). '12' at the lower left is the page number.
There are 5 lines, not 6. The short interior stroke is not a separate line.
